A field toolkit for protection engineers. It connects to Power System Protection Relays over the IEC 61850 MMS protocol to retrieve and analyse COMTRADE fault records, browse an IED\'s live data model, and continuously monitor measurements and alarms across a whole fleet of substations.
Retrieve DFR fault records from a relay over MMS, with Bulk / Single / Deep Scan modes and vendor profiles.
Plot analog and digital channels, measure with T1/T2 cursors, and export the chart or a PDF report.
Browse, open, share, and manage every COMTRADE file already downloaded, organised per folder.
Store substation, bay, IP, brand, and type per relay, with single or bulk ping and CSV import/export.
Browse a live IEC 61850 data model tree (LD / LN / DO / DA) and read real-time values.
Poll monitored points across many IEDs, with alarm thresholds, per-group refresh, and bulk edit.
Define a reusable point set per relay model and apply it to any device of that type in one step.
Export devices, monitored points, and templates into one JSON file, and merge it back without overwriting.
Checks GitHub for new releases, installs them in-app, and can announce them by push notification.
Five colour schemes including the multi-colour Abstract theme, Light/Dark mode, and Indonesian/English.

This guide explains every screen in the app and how to use it. Tap a section below to expand its explanation.
No help topics match your search
Main menu and shortcuts to every feature
The main dashboard shown right after the splash screen. It gives quick-access cards to the app\'s core features and a side menu for settings and other tools.
Opens the side drawer with theme switch, Settings, IED Monitoring, Edit Template, VPN, and About.
Download DFR, File History, DFR Viewer, Relay List, IED Explorer, and IED Monitoring - tap any card to jump straight into that feature.
Substation count, device online status, and active alarm count across the whole fleet, at a glance.
Floating button in the bottom-right corner that opens the About screen.
Opens the Notifications screen. A red dot means there\'s something unread - usually a new app version.

1. Tap any menu card to open that feature directly.\n2. The summary banner below the cards ({ic:location} substations, {ic:list} devices, {ic:warning} active alarms) gives an instant fleet-wide overview - open Relay List or IED Monitoring for the full detail behind these numbers.

1. Tap {ic:menu} in the top-left corner to open the side drawer.\n2. From there you can switch Light/Dark mode and color theme, open Settings, IED Monitoring, or Edit Template, connect to VPN, or view About.
Download COMTRADE (DFR) files from a relay over MMS
Connects to a protection relay via the IEC 61850 MMS protocol to search for and download COMTRADE (DFR) fault-recording files.
Picks a saved relay from the Relay List instead of typing its IP address manually.
Selects the relay protocol profile (Default / ABB-GE / Schneider) before connecting.
Opens an MMS connection to the relay at the entered IP address.
Chooses Bulk (latest files), Single (N-th file), or Deep Scan (search multiple folders), with an N value next to it.
Downloads the selected file from the scan results list into local storage.
1. Enter the relay\'s IP address, or tap {ic:list} to pick a saved device.\n2. Choose a Profile if needed (Default / ABB-GE / Schneider).\n3. Tap CONNECT to open the MMS session.
1. Pick Bulk to list the latest files, Single to jump to the N-th file, or Deep Scan to search multiple folders at once.\n2. Adjust the N value next to the mode when relevant.
1. Tap {ic:download} DOWNLOAD next to a file in the scan results.\n2. The file is saved automatically and can be reopened anytime from Download History.
Browse, open, and manage downloaded DFR files
Local file manager for every COMTRADE file that has been downloaded, organized by folder so past records are easy to find again.
Opens this download folder directly in your phone\'s file manager app.
Tap a folder to open it, or tap a .cfg file to open it directly in DFR Viewer.
Delete or share a file/folder from its menu.
1. Browse folders and files in the list.\n2. Tap a .cfg file to open it directly in DFR Viewer.
1. Open the menu on a file or folder.\n2. Choose {ic:delete} Delete to remove it, or {ic:share} Share to send it to another app.
1. If asked, grant the \'Manage All Files\' permission.\n2. This lets the app show every downloaded file here, not just its own folder.
Manage the relay database: add, ping, import/export CSV
A database of protection relays (substation, bay, device name, IP, brand, and type) so devices don\'t need to be re-entered every time. Includes online/offline ping status.
Bulk-pings every device in the current list at once to check reachability.
Saves the current device list as a CSV backup file.
Loads devices from a CSV file into the database.
Filters the device list by substation (GI) and bay.
Total device count and how many are online, port-open, or offline.
Tap a card to choose an action for that device: Download DFR, IED Explorer, Ping, or Delete.
1. Add a device manually, or tap {ic:import} Import to load a CSV file.\n2. Use Export Template first to see the required column order.
1. Tap PING on a single device card to check it.\n2. Or tap {ic:ping} at the top to bulk-ping every device at once.
1. Tap a device card.\n2. Choose Download DFR, IED Explorer, Ping, or Delete from the popup.
1. Tap {ic:export} Export to save the current device list as a CSV file.
Browse an IED\'s IEC 61850 data model live
Connects live to an IED and lets you browse its full IEC 61850 data model tree (Logical Device, Logical Node, Data Object, Data Attribute), reading real-time values along the way.
Picks a saved relay from the Relay List instead of typing its IP address.
Quick network reachability check before connecting.
Filters the data model tree by name or path.
Opens a dialog to add that data point to IED Monitoring, with a custom name, type (Float/Boolean/String), and - for Float - unit and multiplier.
Rebuilds the data model structure from scratch if it looks outdated.
1. Enter the IP address, or tap {ic:list} to pick from the Relay List.\n2. Tap EXPLORE to connect.
1. Tap a folder row to expand or collapse that branch.\n2. Use {ic:search} the search bar to filter by name or path.

1. Tap the {ic:add} icon next to a value.
2. Set a custom name and pick the type (Float/Boolean/String).
3. For Float, also set the unit and multiplier so the value is scaled and labeled correctly.
4. Tap ADD to save it to IED Monitoring.
1. Tap {ic:sync} to rebuild the structure if it looks outdated.\n2. Tap CLOSE IED to disconnect when finished.
View and analyze COMTRADE waveform recordings
Opens a COMTRADE (.cfg + .dat) file pair and plots its analog and digital channels for fault analysis, with cursors, zoom, and report export.
Locks the zoom level across all channels so they stay in sync while scrolling.
Locks the T1/T2 cursor position across all channels.
Opens a different COMTRADE (.cfg) file manually.
Opens the channel configuration menu to rename, group, or show/hide channels.
1. Open a file from Download History, or tap {ic:folder} to choose one manually.
1. Drag the T1/T2 cursors on the chart.\n2. Read the time and value difference between the two points.
1. Tap {ic:settings} to open the channel menu.\n2. Rename, group, or show/hide channels as needed.
1. Pinch to zoom, or tap {ic:zoom} to lock the zoom level across channels.\n2. Use DOWNLOAD IMG or EXPORT TO PDF to save the chart/report.
Live values and alarms from multiple IEDs at once
Continuously polls a saved list of monitored points across one or more IEDs, grouped by device, with configurable alarm thresholds and a live status indicator per device.
Forces an immediate update of every monitored device at once.
Applies a saved relay template\'s points in bulk to one or more devices.
Quickly finds a point by name when the list is long.
Expands or collapses a device group\'s point list.
Refreshes only that one device group instead of the whole list.
Opens a table to edit name, address, unit, and multiplier for every point in that device group at once, or delete several at once.
Removes an entire device group and all of its monitored points.
Edits a single point: rename it, set unit/multiplier, invert a boolean, or set an Alarm threshold.
1. Add individual points from IED Explorer using its {ic:add} icon.\n2. Or bulk-add a whole relay type\'s points at once with the {ic:template} Template icon in the header - see Edit Template below.
1. Each group header shows a connection dot and the full last-update date/time.\n2. For boolean points, TRUE shows in red and FALSE in green, matching a fault/alarm condition usually being TRUE.
1. Tap {ic:edit} Bulk Edit on a device group header.\n2. Edit name, address, unit, or multiplier for every point at once, or delete several - then tap Save.

1. Tap the {ic:edit} pencil icon on a point.\n2. Rename it, set its unit/multiplier, invert a boolean, or enable an Alarm with a high/low threshold.\n3. When a point breaches its alarm, its value turns red for an at-a-glance warning.
1. Tap {ic:sync} in the header to refresh every device, or pull down the list.\n2. Tap the refresh icon on a single group header to refresh only that device.
Define reusable monitoring point sets per relay type/model

Lets you author and maintain relay templates - a named set of monitoring points (name, IEC 61850 address suffix, type, unit, multiplier) tied to a relay model rather than one physical device. Once defined, a template can be applied to any device of that model from IED Monitoring\'s \"Template\" button, instead of adding every point by hand via IED Explorer.
Duplicates the currently selected template under a new name.
Picks which existing template to view or edit.
Deletes the whole selected template, with confirmation.
Removes a single point row from the table, with confirmation.
Commits field edits, added rows, and deleted rows - required before leaving, otherwise changes are discarded.

1. Tap {ic:add} Add Template to create a new, empty template.\n2. Or tap {ic:copy} next to the spinner to duplicate the selected one under a new name.\n3. Tap {ic:delete} to delete the whole selected template.
1. Fill in each row\'s Name, Address (LD/LN.DO.DA suffix only, no device name), Type, Unit, and Multiplier.\n2. Use Add Row for a new point, and {ic:delete} at the end of a row to remove it.
1. Tap {ic:save} Save to commit field edits, added rows, and deleted rows.\n2. Switching templates or leaving without saving discards them.
1. Go to IED Monitoring.\n2. Tap its Template icon to apply this saved template to one or more devices of that relay model.
MMS port, ping, monitoring interval, language, backup, and more

Configures technical defaults used throughout the app: MMS connection settings, ping behavior, DFR viewer defaults, monitoring update interval, cache, app language, and backing up/restoring the app\'s configuration.
MMS port, ping timeouts, monitoring interval, DFR viewer defaults - each section saves independently.
Frees storage used by cached downloaded structure data.
Switches the whole app between Indonesian and English instantly.
Saves the device list, monitoring points, and relay templates into one JSON backup file.
Merges a previously exported file\'s devices/points/templates into what\'s already on this phone, without overwriting existing entries.
1. Adjust a field.\n2. Tap Save on that section to apply it.
1. Use {ic:delete} Clear Application Cache if downloaded structure caches take up too much storage.\n2. Change Application Language to switch instantly between Indonesian and English.

1. Tap {ic:export} Export Configuration to save everything into one JSON file.\n2. Tap {ic:import} Import Configuration and pick a previously exported file to merge it in - existing entries are never overwritten or deleted.
Shows the app\'s purpose, current version number, and developer credit.
Shows the app\'s purpose, current version number, and developer credit.
1. Open it from the side drawer.\n2. Check which app version you\'re running - useful when reporting an issue.
General notes that apply across the app: how the Intranet/VPN check works, how to switch color themes, and which actions require a network connection to the relay.
Quick reachability check before connecting to a relay; offers to open the FortiClient VPN app if it fails.
Five colour schemes: Modern Blue, Emerald, Purple, Red, and Abstract. The last one (the multi-colour dot) gives each screen its own colour combination instead of one hue everywhere.

1. Toggle the INTRANET switch on a connection screen for a quick reachability check.\n2. If it fails, the app offers to open the {ic:vpn} FortiClient VPN app - also reachable directly from the side drawer.

1. Open the side drawer with {ic:menu}.
2. Tap one of the five colour dots under "Colour Scheme" to change the scheme.
3. Pick the multi-colour dot for the Abstract theme, which rotates the palette per screen.
4. Tap {ic:theme} "Change Mode" to switch between Light and Dark.
1. Most of the app works fully offline.\n2. Only actions that talk to a physical relay (connect, explore, download, monitor, ping) need the phone on the same network as the relay, usually via VPN.
